pins.definition: To perceive someone or something with your eyes.
To notice or perceive something with your eyes.
To perceive with the eyes, or to have the ability to see.

situation: A woman stands in a dimly lit art gallery, lifting a pair of heavy, ornate spectacles to her eyes to examine a painting on the wall.
subject: the act of perceiving with the eyes
brief: A woman stands before a dark canvas in a gallery, and from her open eyes two beams of bright, tangible white light stretch forward like physical glass rods, touching the surface of the painting and making the hidden details glow intensely.
prompt: A woman stands before a dark canvas in a gallery, and from her open eyes two beams of bright, tangible white light stretch forward like physical glass rods, touching the surface of the painting and making the hidden details glow intensely. surrealism in the manner of Magritte and Dalí, one impossible juxtaposition rendered with complete photographic conviction, still air, an empty horizon. One square illustration. The scene is fully rendered and fully inhabited — no silhouettes, no flat icons, no diagram, no empty schematic space. A single subject dominates the frame and everything else is arranged around it. Absolutely no text anywhere in the image: no letters, words, numbers, captions, labels, signage, logos, watermarks or pseudo-text.
